claims.statement: The batibat is a vengeful demon of Ilocano folklore, called bangungot in Tagalog folklore, taking the form of an ancient, grossly obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.
claims.statement_id: Batibat adalah setan pendendam dalam cerita rakyat Ilokano, disebut bangungot dalam cerita rakyat Tagalog, berwujud roh perempuan tua yang sangat gemuk penghuni pohon.
claims.quote: The Batibat is a vengeful demon found in Ilocano folklore. In Tagalog folklore, the creature is called Bangungot. The batibat takes the form of an ancient, grotesquely obese, tree-dwelling female spirit.

claims.statement: Batibat usually meet humans when their trees are felled, especially when made into a house post, and then inhabit what is left of the tree.
claims.statement_id: Batibat biasanya bersentuhan dengan manusia ketika pohonnya ditebang, terutama bila dijadikan tiang rumah, lalu ia menghuni sisa pohonnya.
claims.quote: They usually come in contact with humans when the trees in which they reside are felled and are made homeless, especially when their tree is made into a support post for a house.

claims.statement: The batibat forbids sleeping near its post; if someone does, it takes its true form, smothers the victim and invades their dreams, causing sleep paralysis and nightmares; hence the Ilocano word batíbat for nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Batibat melarang manusia tidur di dekat tiangnya; bila ada yang tidur di sana, ia berubah ke wujud aslinya, menindih korban dan memasuki mimpinya hingga terjadi ketindihan dan mimpi buruk; dari sinilah kata Ilokano batíbat untuk mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: When a person does sleep near it, the batibat transforms into its true form and attacks the person by suffocating their victim and invading their dream space, causing sleep paralysis and waking nightmares. This condition lends itself to the Ilocano word for nightmare, "batíbat"

claims.statement: To ward off the batibat, bite your thumb or wiggle your toes to wake from the nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menangkal batibat, orang dianjurkan menggigit ibu jari atau menggerakkan jari kaki agar terbangun dari mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: To ward off the batibat, one should bite one's thumb or wiggle one's toes. In this way, the person will awaken from the nightmare induced by the batibat.

claims.statement: The creature appears in the fifth episode of the Netflix series Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, played by Megan Leitch.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini muncul dalam episode kelima serial Netflix Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, diperankan Megan Leitch.
claims.quote: The creature appears in the fifth episode of the Netflix series Chilling Adventures of Sabrina, played by Megan Leitch.

claims.statement: The 2020 horror film Evil Takes Root: The Curse of the Batibat features one of these creatures.
claims.statement_id: Film horor Evil Takes Root: The Curse of the Batibat (2020) menampilkan makhluk ini.
claims.quote: The 2020 horror film Evil Takes Root: The Curse of the Batibat features one of these creatures.

claims.statement: The bungisngis is a one-eyed giant of Philippine folklore said to live in Meluz, Orion, Bataan and Batangas and always laughing; its name comes from Cebuano ngisi, 'to giggle'.
claims.statement_id: Bungisngis adalah raksasa bermata satu dalam cerita rakyat Filipina yang konon tinggal di Meluz, Orion, Bataan, dan Batangas dan selalu tertawa; namanya berasal dari kata Cebuano ngisi, 'terkikik'.
claims.quote: Bungisngis is a one-eyed giant in Philippine folklore. This giant, purported to dwell in Meluz, Orion, Bataan and Batangas and is described as always laughing. The literal meaning of the name Bungingis is derived from the Cebuano word ngisi which means "to giggle".

claims.statement: This humanlike giant has always-visible large teeth, an upper lip covering its face when thrown back, two long tusks, and a single mid-forehead eye offset by sharp hearing.
claims.statement_id: Raksasa berwujud manusia ini bergigi besar yang selalu terlihat, bibir atasnya menutupi wajah saat mendongak, dua taring panjang mencuat dari mulutnya, dan satu-satunya matanya di tengah dahi diimbangi pendengaran tajam.
claims.quote: Having a humanoid shape, it has large teeth which are always showing, and its upper lip covers its face when it is thrown back. Two long tusks protrude from the sides of its mouth. The giant's only eye is found in the middle of its forehead, but this is compensated for by its strong sense of hearing.

claims.statement: In the Filipino tale The Three Friends: the Monkey, the Dog and the Carabao, the giant lifts the carabao and throws it knee-deep into the ground; though strong, it is easily outwitted and panics, and the Monkey's tricks lead to its death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Filipina Tiga Sahabat: Monyet, Anjing, dan Kerbau, raksasa ini mengangkat kerbau dan melemparnya hingga terbenam sampai lutut; meski kuat, bungisngis mudah diakali dan cepat panik, dan tipu daya Monyet membawanya pada kematian.
claims.quote: In the Filipino tale "The Three Friends – The Monkey, The Dog and The Carabao," the giant is able to lift the carabao and throw it with such force that it lands knee-deep in the ground. However, despite its strength, the bungisngis is easily outwitted and quickly panics.

claims.statement: Cha kla (จะกละ) or Phi Cha kla is a spirit of Thai folklore resembling a wild cat, believed to be a malevolent spirit raised and controlled by warlocks to harm enemies; in southern Thailand it is called phi luang.
claims.statement_id: Cha kla (จะกละ) atau Phi Cha kla adalah roh dalam cerita rakyat Thailand yang menyerupai kucing liar, diyakini roh jahat yang dipelihara dan dikendalikan penyihir untuk mencelakai musuh; di Thailand selatan disebut phi luang.
claims.quote: or Phi Cha kla (ผีจะกละ, pronounced [pʰiː t͡ɕà kà.lá]) is a type of spirit in Thai folklore, said to resemble a wild cat. It is believed to be a malevolent spirit raised and controlled by warlocks to harm their enemies. In the southern regions of Thailand, it is known as phi luang

claims.statement: Cha kla is recorded in the Ayutthaya-period Three Seals Law Code, over 300 years old, alongside beings such as the krasue, under the name cha la.
claims.statement_id: Cha kla tercatat dalam Hukum Tiga Segel dari masa Ayutthaya, lebih dari 300 tahun lalu, bersama makhluk gaib lain seperti krasue, dengan nama cha la.
claims.quote: It is documented in the Three Seals Law Code dating back over 300 years to the Ayutthaya period, where it is listed alongside other supernatural beings such as the Krasue. In the text, it is referred to as Cha la

claims.statement: Cha kla's fur is pitch black, coarse and dull, growing backwards upward and forward, its eyes blood-red; it emerges only at night, fears humans and flees to its burrow when seen.
claims.statement_id: Bulu cha kla hitam pekat, kasar, dan kusam, tumbuh terbalik ke atas dan ke depan, matanya merah seperti darah; ia hanya keluar malam hari, takut manusia, dan lari ke liangnya bila terlihat.
claims.quote: However, its fur is pitch black with a coarse texture, lacking any shine. The hairs grow in reverse, flaring upward and forward. Its eyes glow deep red, like blood. Nocturnal by nature, Cha kla emerges only at night. It fears humans

claims.statement: According to legend, cha kla has a deadly aura; merely seeing or touching it can cause death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, cha kla memiliki aura mematikan; melihat atau menyentuhnya saja dapat menyebabkan kematian.
claims.quote: According to legend, Cha kla possesses a deadly aura. Even the mere sight or touch of it can cause death.

claims.statement: Khamot (โขมด) is a ghost of Thai folklore; its name is borrowed from Khmer khmaoch, 'ghost in general', and it is considered related to the krasue and phong ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Khamot (โขมด) adalah hantu dalam cerita rakyat Thailand; namanya dipinjam dari kata Khmer khmaoch, 'hantu secara umum', dan ia dianggap berkerabat dengan krasue dan hantu phong.
claims.quote: is a type of ghost in Thai folklore. The term is borrowed from the Khmer word khmaoch

claims.statement: In some accounts khamot appears as a floating, flickering light at night, especially in damp or marshy areas, misleading forest travellers into thinking someone ahead carries a torch or there is a fire; approached, it vanishes and reappears all around.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian kisah khamot tampak sebagai bola cahaya melayang yang berkedip di malam hari, terutama di daerah lembap atau berawa, dan menyesatkan pengembara di hutan seolah ada orang membawa obor atau api di depan; saat didekati cahaya itu lenyap lalu muncul mengelilingi.
claims.quote: In some accounts, it appears as a floating ball of light, a large flickering glow seen at night, especially in damp or marshy areas. It is said to lure travelers in the forest into losing their way, making them believe that someone ahead is carrying a torch or that there is a fire.

claims.statement: Per the Royal Institute Dictionary, the phenomenon is scientifically explained as methane from decaying organic matter igniting in the air; it also groups khamot with the krasue and phong ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kamus Royal Institute, secara ilmiah gejala ini dijelaskan sebagai gas metana dari pembusukan bahan organik yang dapat menyala di udara; kamus itu juga menggolongkan khamot bersama krasue dan hantu phong.
claims.quote: Scientifically, this phenomenon is explained as methane gas produced by the decomposition of organic matter, which can ignite in the air and appear as flickering lights in the dark.

claims.statement: In some regions khamot is a forest spirit seen as floating light; in others a malevolent ghost deceiving travellers by shapeshifting.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa daerah khamot dianggap roh hutan berupa cahaya melayang, di daerah lain hantu jahat yang menipu pengembara dengan berganti wujud.
claims.quote: In others, it is considered a malevolent ghost that deceives and haunts travelers by shapeshifting into various forms.

claims.statement: In Lamphun, northern Thailand, the Loy Khamot tradition is held at the twelfth lunar month's full moon, coinciding with Loy Krathong, with floating lanterns sparkling like khamot's lights.
claims.statement_id: Di Provinsi Lamphun, Thailand utara, ada tradisi Loy Khamot pada purnama bulan kedua belas, bertepatan dengan Loy Krathong, dengan lentera terapung yang berkilau seperti cahaya khamot.
claims.quote: In Lamphun province, northern Thailand, there is a local tradition called Loy Khamot (ลอยโขมด), held during the full moon of the twelfth lunar month, which coincides with the Loy Krathong festival

claims.statement: The mandurugo is a mythical being of Philippine folklore similar to a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Mandurugo adalah makhluk mitos dari cerita rakyat Filipina yang mirip vampir.
claims.quote: The Mandurugo is a mythical being from Philippine folklore, similar to a vampire.

claims.statement: The mandurugo, a variety of aswang, is usually a young beautiful woman by day but at night grows wings and a long sharp tongue to cut a man's neck or prick his mouth while kissing to get blood.
claims.statement_id: Mandurugo, sejenis aswang, pada siang hari biasanya perempuan muda cantik, tetapi pada malam hari menumbuhkan sayap dan lidah panjang tajam untuk melukai leher laki-laki atau menusuk mulutnya saat berciuman demi darah.
claims.quote: A variety of Aswang (Filipino shapeshifter), the Mandurugo resembles a vampire. They are usually young and beautiful women by day, but develop wings and long, sharp tongues by night, which they use to either make cuts in a man's neck, or prick the inside of his mouth while kissing him to obtain blood.

claims.statement: Its stories, popular among Tagalog and Bicol speakers, vary; sometimes it marries men to prey on them, or keeps one husband as cover and flies to other villages to feed.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya populer di kalangan penutur Tagalog dan Bicol dan bervariasi; kadang mandurugo menikahi laki-laki untuk dimangsa, atau memilih satu suami sebagai kedok lalu terbang ke desa lain untuk makan.
claims.quote: The stories, popular to Tagalog and Bicol speakers, have many variations. Sometimes the Mandurugo marries unsuspecting men to prey upon them, or may just select one husband, using him as a cover for her blood drinking activities, flying to other villages to feed.

claims.statement: In The Girl With Many Loves, the fourth husband keeps a knife, feels a prick on his neck, stabs the creature above him, and next day his wife is found dead with a knife wound in her chest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Gadis dengan Banyak Cinta, suami keempat berjaga dengan pisau, merasakan tusukan di leher, menikam makhluk di atasnya, dan esoknya istrinya ditemukan tewas dengan luka tusuk di dada.
claims.quote: The fourth husband, fearing the same fate as his predecessors, is afraid to sleep at night and holds a knife in his hand. A little after midnight, the man senses something over him before feeling a prick on his neck. He stabs at the creature on top of him and hears a loud screech and the flapping of wings. The next day, his wife is found dead

claims.statement: Films such as The Vampire People (1966) were products of vampire folklore and mainstream culture.
claims.statement_id: Film seperti The Vampire People (1966) lahir dari cerita rakyat vampir dan budaya arus utama.
claims.quote: Films such as The Vampire People (1966) were the product of vampire folklore and mainstream culture.
